faces.summary: Liveness probe of this stone and its wire protocol marker.
This route table - every surface, described in place.
Me: my frame, sung full-voice (the SelfView projection).
Me, spelled explicitly (same SelfView).
A stone by name or id: mine answered here; others answer 404 with a Location to their home stone (the garden's only true redirect).
Local data (L22): this moss's live counters - ingest, dispatch, topology, offerings.
Garden data (L22): the room as this moss sees it - self spliced among the peers, every row a canonical frame.
The catalog this stone can place from (derived).
This stone's banks, plus the removable volumes ready for adoption.
The adopt ceremony: {device: mount point, name: bank FQN} - writes the manifest onto the drive and sings the news (ADR-0005 sec 8).
Eject a bank by name: authoritative absence, sung to the room (ADR-0005 sec 8.3).
Declare a bank's roles: {roles: [sink]} - a sink receives checkpoints (ADR-0005 sec 4).
List a bank directory (optional ?path= subdirectory): the files riding the volume, minus the adoption record. A bank held by a peer answers the garden's redirect (knows_at).
Read one file from a bank: the raw bytes, content-type guessed from the extension; the path is relative to the bank's root. A peer's bank answers the garden's redirect (knows_at).
Write one file onto a bank: the raw body, parent directories created - makes a sink a real storage destination. A peer's bank answers the garden's redirect (knows_at); writes bind at their authority.
Delete one file from a bank. Directories refuse - wholesale removal is the operator's hand. A peer's bank answers the garden's redirect.
Move (rename) one file within a bank: {move_to: path} - no re-upload. Never overwrites. A peer's bank answers the garden's redirect.
Follow an offering's logs: history first (tail=N bounds it), then live - SSE `log` events, one JSON line each. A peer's offering answers the garden's redirect.
Run this offering's declared will: Phase A imprint (quiesce -> copy -> resume), then pack, ferry, commit.
The last capture run of this offering: phase, checkpoint, ferried sinks.
Replant from a checkpoint {run?}: verify, restore the directory, place from the stored spec - same FQN, same connection strings (ADR-0005 §6).
Every async operation on this stone, newest first.
One job by id: kind, subject, status, error, result.
This stone's living landing page: identity, offerings, banks, the room.
Lands on the portrait.
The live page: stones, offerings, and the event ring as they happen.
SSE firehose: topology events (seen/goodbye/expired) and offering changes.
Garden data (L22): every bank in the room, self included, from the one cache.
Every offering placed on this stone (the collection).
Plant a managed offering {image?, ports:{name:container}, runtime?, inputs?}; catalog name wins when one exists.
The placed record - plan, decisions, ports (OFFERINGS.md §5.3).
Rest a managed offering - stopped, and reconcile will keep it so.
Wake a rested offering; resurrects from its stored spec if reality lost it.
Uproot - remove the workload and forget the offering.

Announcement.description:
One garden datagram, decoded. `data` stays opaque here — typed bodies
(`chirp::ChirpBody`) are parsed by the handler that registered for the
`kind` (R2.9).

data.description: Opaque payload — the handler that claimed this type gives it meaning.

msg_id.description:
Time-ordered identity of this datagram; receivers dedup on it for
[`crate::consts::DEDUP_TTL_SECS`]. v1 always sets it; the PoC allowed
absence (such datagrams bypass dedup — a PoC quirk we do not inherit).

sender_cert.description: Signer certificate (PEM) — future; v1 emits unsigned.

signature.description: Pond signature (base64) — future; v1 emits unsigned.

Announcement.title: Announcement

BankEntry.description:
One storage bank in presence (ADR-0005 §8): logical FQN identity plus
the physical device, its state, and roles. Capacity/used are TELEMETRY —
they never trigger frames, they ride along (§8.2's anti-spam law); both
are optional because "unknown" is honest.

fqn.description:
Logical bank identity, FQN per ADR-0003 (`bank::default` communal,
explicit instances private).

roles.description: Declared roles (sink today; the set grows with ADR-0005's tiers).

FrameMeta.description: Frame housekeeping: schema identity and ordering.

boot_id.description: Identity of this boot — peers distinguish restart from heartbeat.

part.description:
Quantization position when one announcement spans several frames
(ADR-0004 A2.3). Purely informational: consumers never wait or
reassemble — revs make every frame independently mergeable.

proto.description: Wire schema marker; [`crate::consts::PROTO_V1`] when spoken by v1.

seq.description: Monotonic chirp counter for this boot — gap detection, ordering.

Inventory.description:
A domain inventory block: capped items, declared totals, one revision.
The unit of the inventory map (A2.1) and of framer quantization (A2.3):
a block rides WHOLE or waits — partial item lists are forbidden.

rev.description:
Monotonic per-boot generation of this domain's set. The merge
function: frames compare revisions, mismatches heal by rich ask.

total.description:
Total items hosted when `items` is truncated to the wire cap;
absent = everything fit (truncation declared, never silent).

Inventory2.description:
A domain inventory block: capped items, declared totals, one revision.
The unit of the inventory map (A2.1) and of framer quantization (A2.3):
a block rides WHOLE or waits — partial item lists are forbidden.

rev.description:
Monotonic per-boot generation of this domain's set. The merge
function: frames compare revisions, mismatches heal by rich ask.

total.description:
Total items hosted when `items` is truncated to the wire cap;
absent = everything fit (truncation declared, never silent).

InventoryMap.description:
The inventory MAP (ADR-0004 A2.1): rootspace of the frame is closed;
garden domains enter here as blocks. Known domains are compile-time
fields; unknown domains from newer stones round-trip losslessly through
the passthrough map (older stones relay without destroying).

Moss.description: Software identity of the resident daemon.

Network.description: Everything needed to open a connection — and to wake it later.

address.description: LAN-routable address of the HTTP surface.

mac.description: MAC for wake-on-LAN; absent where unknown.

Part.description: Position of this frame within a multi-frame announcement.

PeerAddress.description: How to reach a stone's HTTP surface.

tls_port.description: HTTPS port when pond security is active; absent otherwise.

Presence.description: The frame's claims about right now.

Reception.description:
Reception facts: when WE first/last heard from this stone. Senders emit
placeholders; every listener overwrites both — they describe the
relationship, not the speaker.

ServiceEntry.description:
One offering a stone runs, as seen in presence. Identity fields speak
FQN verbatim (ADR-0003); moniker suppression is a rendering concern.

offering_id.description: Stable identity of the offering instance; survives renames.

ports.description:
Actual host ports by name ("default", "management"...) — populated
only where remapped from manifest defaults (PORT-0001 inherited).
Absent/empty = defaults stand.

state.description: How the instance is doing: runtime status + orchestration role.

stem.description: Catalog stem this instance was planted from (provenance).

ServiceState.description: Runtime condition of one offering instance.

role.description: Orchestration role when active: primary | replica | joining.

Stone.description: The speaking stone: identity and reachability. Immutable across a boot.

name.description: Human-facing name; also the mDNS label.

network.description: How to reach it, plus wake-on-LAN material.

ChirpFrame.description:
The garden frame: one canonical shape spoken on the wire, held in the
topology cache, and projected by HTTP surfaces. Sections, not a flat
field zoo. (No Default: a frame without a speaking stone is meaningless.)

inventory.description: Its inventory domains (services today; banks next; unknown preserved).

received.description: Reception facts — senders emit placeholders, listeners overwrite.

ChirpFrame.title: ChirpFrame

DiscoveryRequest.description: What a discovery request asks for. `"moss"` finds stones ([`TARGET_MOSS`]).

discover.description: What kind of speaker we are looking for.

request_id.description: Echoed by responders' logs; correlates one round of answers.

requester.description: Who is asking (a stone name or client label).

rich.description:
Rich ask (ADR-0004 §1): responders include their service inventory
so a newcomer populates its cache in one exchange. Absent from the
wire while false — legacy request bytes stay lean.

DiscoveryRequest.title: DiscoveryRequest

DiscoveryResponse.description:
Where a willing respondent lives, and (when the ask was rich) what it
hosts. The `stone:` block always answers "who are you"; the inventory
MAP answers "what do you have" — every domain, identical shapes to the
chirp frame's (A2.1: the revision vector is a shape, not a field list).

inventory.description:
The full inventory map, iff the request carried rich:true — services
AND banks AND whatever domains the future brings (W7 finding: a
newcomer learns the whole room in one exchange).

lantern_endpoint.description: Legacy Lantern registry endpoint (v0 field; v1 emits absent).

stone.description: WHO answered: identity and reachability (frame's `stone:` block).

DiscoveryResponse.title: DiscoveryResponse
